(S.C.C.H. - 1)
 Dated this the 17th day of January, 2024

Present: Smt. B.V. Renuka, B.Sc., Ll.B.,
 Chief Judge
 Member, Prl. M.A.C.T., Bengaluru.

Petitioner: Hoysala H.N.,
 S/o. Nanjappa,
 Aged about 45 years,

 Holenarasipura Town,
 Holenarasipura Bazar,

(Represented by Sri C.C.Harish,

 -Vs-
Respondents: 1. H.P.Nethra,
 W/o.Late K.C.Revanna,

(R.C.Owner of motorcycle bearing
 Reg.No.KA-45-J-3495)

 Regional office, No.5th & 6th floor,
 Krishi Bhavan, Hudson Circle,
 Nrupathunga Road,

(Policy No.0706023118P112180693
 Valid from 27.12.2018 to 26.12.2019)
Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024

1

(Represented by Sri H.A.Kumara  Swamy , Advocate)
 JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

2. Briefly stated, the case of the petitioner is as follows:
That on 09.12.2019 at about 4.30 p.m. when the petitioner was proceeding in Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J-3495 as a pillion rider and one Lakshmana was the rider and when they reached near Chowdeshwari petrol bunk,
B.M.Road, Channarayapatna town, Hasan district , the rider of the Honda Activa scooter drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He took treatment in Government hospital and in Punya hospital, Channarayapatna.
A case was registered in Crime No.157/2019 against the rider of Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J-3495 at Channarayapatna Traffic police station.
Hence, this petition for compensation.
3. In response to the notice of the petition, the respondent No.1 has not chosen to appear before the Court and he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 has appeared through its advocate and has filed written statement by denying the petition averments as false.
The issuance of policy in respect of Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J- 3495 is admitted and the liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
The policy issued is 'Liability only policy' and hence, the pillion rider is not entitled for any compensation as per the terms and conditions of the policy.
The first respondent has not submitted the claim form and other documents like R.C., F.C. and D.L. for verification .
The rider of the motorcycle drove the same without having valid and effective driving licence which is in contravention of the policy conditions.
The compensation claimed is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-45-J- 3495 by its rider dashed to the petitioner who was proceeding as pillion rider in the above motorcycle and he sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 09.12.2019?

Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
2 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order?
5. On behalf of the petitioner, he examined himself as PW-1 and one witness is examined as PW-2 and got marked Exhibits P.1 to P.14.
The respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW1 and got marked two documents at Ex.R.1 and R.2.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides.
7.

My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly in affirmative, compensation of Rs.3,55,000/ - from the respondents Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 8. Issue No.1: The petitioner in order to prove this issue has placed reliance on his evidence and documentary evidence as per Exs.P.1 to P.7 and P.12 such as FIR with complaint, spot panchanama,
spot sketch, seizure panchanama , IMV report, chargesheet, wound certificate and MLC extract.
PW-1 being the petitioner and the injured in his affidavit evidence has narrated how he has met with an accident and the accident was due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J-3495.
The owner of the Honda Activa scooter in question has remained exparte.

The second respondent in its written statement has denied the involvement of the insured vehicle and also the negligence aspect on the ground that the petitioner in order to get compensation in collusion with the police has falsely implicated the Honda Activa scooter in question by lodging false complaint against the rider of the Honda Activa scooter after the lapse of 3 days of the alleged accident.
Let us consider the evidence on record to decide this issue.

9. FIR as per Ex.P.1 discloses that on the basis of the complaint lodged by Dr.Geetha , who is the wife of the petitioner, a criminal case was registered against the rider of Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J- 3495 .

As per the said document accident occurred on 09.12.2019 ,
but the complaint was lodged on 11.12.2019.
He admits that after two days of the accident his wife has lodged the complaint.
That means after providing treatment to the petitioner, his wife has lodged the complaint.
Thus, there is two days delay in lodging the complaint.

In Ex.P.1, it is mentioned that immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government hospital ,
Channarayapatna and after first aid he was shifted to Punya hospital , Channrayapatna and thereafter his wife has lodged the complaint to the police.
PW1 has denied that in the accident he has sustained only simple injuries and as such complaint was not lodged immediately on the date of accident.
Merely because there is delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint, the claim of the petitioner cannot be doubted when the complainant has given the plausible explanation for the said delay.

The Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
3 complainant has given prime importance to provide treatment to the petitioner rather than to visit the police station to lodge the complaint.
Such being the case, I am of the opinion that merely because there is delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint, the false implication of the insured vehicle cannot be inferred 10.
PW1 has produced certified copy of M.L.C.Extract as per Ex.P.12, wherein the history of RTA is mentioned as Trauma by bike.
The said document discloses that on the date of accident itself, the petitioner was admitted to Punya hospital , Channarayapatna by his wife i.e, the complainant.

As Ex.P.12 discloses that the petitioner was admitted to Punya hospital on the date of accident itself , it can be safely held that the petitioner met with an accident by Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J- 3495 and he sustained injuries in the accident.
Hence, by considering Ex.P.12 also, it can be safely held that there is no false implication of insured vehicle by the petitioner in collusion with the police as contended by the second respondent.
11. Exhibits P.2 and P.3 are the spot mahazar and spot sketch which reveals the state of affairs at the accident spot.

As per PW-1, on 09.12.2019 at about 4.30 p.m. when he was proceeding in a Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J-3495 as a pillion rider, the rider of the said motorcycle by name Lakshmana rode it in a rash and negligent manner near Chowdeshwari Petrol Bunk, B.M.Road, Channarayapatna and caused the accident.
Ex.P.2 discloses that the accident took place near Chowdeshwari petrol bunk situated on B.M.Road , Channarayapatna town.

As per this document, the place of accident is 6 feet away from the edge of the road towards western side and the width of the B.M.Road is about 33x33 feet and there is a divider in the middle of the said road.
In Ex.P.3, the place of accident is shown about 6 feet away from the edge of the road.

Hence, by considering Exhibits P.2 and P.3, it can be safely held that accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J-3495.
12.

Exs.P.4 and P.5 are the seizure mahazar and IMV Report wherein Honda Activa scooter involved in the accident was seized by police and it was inspected by IMV Inspector and no damages were found on the said scooter.

Even the police intimation which is in the case sheet - Ex.P.11 discloses that on the date of accident itself the hospital authorities of Punya hospital have intimated about the admission of the petitioner with a history of RTA by bike .
Hence, even from this document it can be safely held that the petitioner met with an accident and sustained injuries.
It is the duty of the police to visit the hospital to record the statement of the petitioner after receiving the intimation from the hospital authorities, but the police have not done so.
13. Wound certificate -Ex.P.7 discloses that the petitioner has sustained grievous and simple injuries in the accident.
Ex.P.6 is the chargesheet filed by the police against the rider of Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J-3495 after detailed investigation.
The first respondent being the owner of the said scooter has remained exparte.
The rider of the said scooter has not challenged the chargesheet filed against him.
This conduct of the rider of the scooter in question enables the Court to draw an adverse inference against him that as the accident took place due to his negligent act, he has remained silent.
The entire evidence placed by the petitioner remained unrebutted.
The second respondent has examined its official as RW1.

RW1 has denied the alleged Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
4 accident due to lodging of the complaint after 3 days of the alleged accident.

But as discussed above,
the materials placed on record clearly establish that the insured scooter was involved in the accident and the petitioner has sustained injuries on account of accident caused by the rider of the said Honda Activa scooter.

Hence, by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has proved that he met with an accident due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J-3495 wherein the petitioner was a pillion rider.
Accordingly, I answer this issue in the affirmative.

14. ISSUE No.2:
(a). Pain and Agony:

PW-1 has produced the wound Certificate issued by Punya Hospital at Ex.P.7, which discloses that the petitioner has sustained (1) Pain and swelling in the left knee (2)
pain and swelling in the left leg (3) Multiple abrasion over face.
X-ray shows comminuted fracture of upper end of tibia left.

As per the opinion of the Doctor,
injuries No.1 and 2 are grievous in nature and injury No.3 is simple in nature.

Discharge summary at Ex.P.8 and case sheet at Ex.P.11 disclose that the petitioner had taken treatment in Punya hospital as an inpatient from 09.12.2019 to 19.12.2019 and he has undergone surgery for the fracture with closed reduction with internal fixation.
X
-rays and CT scan films as per Exs.P.13 and P.14 confirms the sustaining of the fracture by the petitioner in accident.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner requires 3 months treatment.
During the treatment period, the petitioner has suffered lot of pain and agony.

So, taking into account the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and number of days of his treatment in the hospital, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

(b). Medical Expenses (including conveyance, attendant charges and extra nourishment):
PW-1 has deposed that he has spent more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental expenses.
In support of his evidence PW-1 has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.9.
These bills are amounting to Rs.1,11,094/-.
) is the final inpatient bill of Punya hospital amounting to Rs.74,800/- .
This bill discloses that the petitioner has paid the said amount towards his treatment in Punya hospital.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for the said amount towards hospital charges.
) is the bill in respect of the implants purchased from Medi Ortho Line for Rs.26,250/-.
PW1 was cross-examined by the second respondent counsel on this bill.
PW1 admits that the said bill is a credit bill and he has not produced the receipt to show that he has paid the amount mentioned in that bill .

Merely because Ex.P.9(22) is a credit bill and merely because the petitioner has not produced any receipt to show that he has paid the said amount, it cannot be said that the petitioner has not purchased the implants as mentioned in that bill since the medical records discloses that the petitioner has undergone surgery by fixation of Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
5 implants at the fracture site.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.26,250/- as mentioned in Ex.P.9(22).
The other bills are pharmacy bills.
These bills are not supported by prescriptions.
Moreover, these bills do not contain the signature of the person who has issued them and the seal of the shop.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the petitioner has spent the amount mentioned in pharmacy bills towards medicines.

However, by considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the type of treatment undergone by the petitioner , it can be said that the petitioner has spent some amount towards medicines, conveyance , attendant charges.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- under this head.
(c) Loss of income during the treatment period:
PW-1 has deposed that prior to the accident he was working as a Doctor and earning Rs.50,000/p.m., PW 1 in his cross-examination has deposed that he is a doctor having specialization in Anaesthesia .
Except the oral assertion of PW1, there is no proof of avocation and income of the petitioner.

However, in view of the suggestion made to PW2, who is the Doctor of Punya hospital that the petitioner is his colleague,
it can be safely held that the petitioner is a Doctor at Punya hospital.
In the absence of any materials in proof of the income of the petitioner, average income of the petitioner is taken at Rs.30,000/p.m.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner requires minimum 3 months treatment.
During that period, the petitioner was unable to do any work and he has suffered loss of income.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.90,000/- under the head loss of income during the period of treatment.
(d) Future loss of earning capacity:

PW-1 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he is getting unbearable pain often, he cannot walk, he has disfigurement and undergoing deep mental shock and getting giddiness and he cannot concentrate on his work and fracture is not united and he has sustained permanent disability.
In order to prove the disability the petitioner has examined the Doctor as PW2.
PW2 in his evidence has deposed about the injuries sustained by the petitioner and nature of treatment undergone by the petitioner.
According to PW2, the petitioner suffers from partial and permanent disability to left lower limb at 39.75%.
Whether the disability assessed by PW2 is to be accepted or not has to be scrutinized cautiously.
PW2 in his cross-examination has deposed that he has treated the petitioner and he has conducted operation on 10.12.2019.
As PW2 is the treated doctor, his evidence has to be believed, but we have to decide whether the disability stated by PW2 amounts to functional disability or not.
As per the admissions of PW2, he has not assessed the whole body disability and functional disability and the petitioner is a Government Doctor and even now the petitioner is working in his hospital.

From Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
6
these versions of PW2, it is clear that even after the accident, the petitioner is working as a Doctor and he is getting income from his profession.
As such the disability stated by PW2 will not amount to functional disability.
However, the disability stated by PW2 may cause unhappiness to the petitioner while doing his profession and also his normal activities .
As such no amount is awarded under this head.
(e) Future Medical Expenses:
PW-2 has deposed that the petitioner requires one more surgery which may cost Rs.70,000/- to Rs.1,00,000/- in his hospital.
PW1 has also deposed that the Doctor has advised him to undergo one more operation which incurs huge expenses.
The medical records disclose that the petitioner has undergone surgery by fixation of implants.
Hence, it can be said that the petitioner requires some amount towards future medical expenses for removal of implants.
As such, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.25,000/- under this head which shall not carry any interest.
(f) Towards unhappiness and loss of amenities:

PW-1 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he is getting unbearable pain often, he cannot walk, he has disfigurement and undergoing deep mental shock and getting giddiness and he cannot concentrate on his work and fracture is not united and he has sustained permanent disability.

PW2 has deposed that the petitioner is having difficulty to walk, sit, squat and climb stairs, there is restriction of movements of ankle joint and knee and the petitioner walks with limping gait and the petitioner is having difficulty in carrying weight and walking and the petitioner suffers from partial and permanent disability to the left lower limb at 39.75% .

By considering the difficulties stated by PWs 1 and 2, it can be safely held that the petitioner suffers from unhappiness to some extent while doing his normal activities and also while doing his avocation.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.70,000/- under this head of unhappiness and loss of amenities.

15. In view of the reasons stated above, in all the petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
 Sl. Head of Compensation Amount  No.
 a. Pain and Agony Rs. 50,000-00  b. Medical Expenses Rs. 1,20,000-00  (conveyance, nourishment  and attendant charges )
 c. Loss of income during the Rs. 90,000-00  treatment and rest period  d. Future Medical Expenses Rs. 25,000-00 Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
7  e. Unhappiness and loss of Rs. 70,000-00  amenities  TOTAL Rs. 3,55,000-00
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,55,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on Rs.3,30,000/- from the date of the petition till deposit in Court.

16. So far as the liability is concerned, according to the petitioner, the first respondent is the owner and the second respondent is the insurer of Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J-3495.
The first respondent being the owner has remained exparte.

The second respondent being the insurer though admits that it has issued the insurance policy in favour of the first respondent relating to Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J-3495 , but it has contended that as the policy issued by it is a 'Liability only Policy', the pillion rider is not entitled for any compensation as per the policy conditions.

In this regard, second respondent has placed the evidence its official as RW1 and RW1 has produced the copy of the insurance policy as per Ex.R.2.
17.
RW1 was cross-examined by the petitioner counsel on Ex.R.2.
On perusal of Ex.R.2, it is clear that it is a 'Liability only Policy' issued in the name of first respondent relating to the Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-45-J-3495 .
The said policy was valid from 27.12.2018 to 26.12.2019.

The schedule of the premium reads as under:
 Basic TP 720-00  Total 720-00  Add: compulsory PA for owner 750-00  driver  PA for unnamed persons 140-00  Sub total (Additions) 890-00  Gross TP 1,610-00  Total Liability premium 1,610-00
Hence, as per the above schedule, it is evident that the premium is collected not only in respect of owner driver, but also in respect of unnamed persons.
RW-1 in his cross- examination has admitted that 'Liability only Policy' covers the risk of the third party , but he has denied that the pillion rider comes under third party.
Even, he has admitted that in the policy he has taken premium of Rs.140/- towards P.A. unnamed person, but he has denied that pillion rider comes under unnamed person in the policy.

As per the version of RW1 in the cross-examination,
unnamed person means the person who moves on the two wheeler i.e., either the rider or the pillion rider of the two wheeler.

From these versions of RW1, it is clear that the premium paid on unnamed Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
8 persons covers the risk of pillion rider of the two wheeler.

18. In this case the petitioner met with an accident when he was moving as a pillion rider on Honda Activa Scooter in question due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the said scooter.

Though the policy as per Ex.R.2 is issued as 'Liability only Policy', but the fact that premium has been collected in respect risk of unnamed persons enables the Court to hold that the petitioner who was a pillion rider on the date of accident in the insured scooter comes under unnamed person.
It is pertinent to note that the term 3rd party includes a party other than those who are the parties to the contract of insurance i.e., insurer is one party and the insured is the other party.
Any person other than the two parties comes under the description of 3rd party.
In the present case also, the petitioner is a third party as respondents No.1 and 2 are the parties to the contract of insurance under Ex.R.2.
The seating capacity in Honda Activa scooter is only two.
Such being the case, the premium of Rs.140/- paid by the insured towards unnamed person in Ex.R.2 is in respect of the pillion rider of the insured scooter.

In view of the version of RW1 that unnamed person means either the rider or the pillion rider of the two wheeler, I am of the opinion that the policy Ex.R.2 covers the risk of the petitioner who was a pillion rider on the insured scooter on the date of accident.

19. If no additional premium was collected by the second respondent company from the first respondent, then the contention of the second respondent that the risk of pillion rider i.e., the petitioner is not covered under the policy would have been considered.
But the situation is not so in the present case, since the second respondent company has collected additional premium towards the risk of unnamed persons.

Hence, by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that the contention of the second respondent that the petitioner is not entitled for compensation as the insurance policy issued in favour of the first respondent is a 'Liability only policy' cannot be accepted.

20. As discussed above, this Court has come to the conclusion that as additional premium has been collected by the second respondent company with respect to an unnamed person under Ex.R.2 , the petitioner who was a pillion rider on the date of accident comes under unnamed person and the risk of the petitioner was covered under the policy Ex.R.2 and as such he is entitled for compensation.
Ex.R.2 was valid as on the date of accident since the accident took place on 09.12.2019.

Merely, on the nomenclature of the policy as 'Liability only Policy', the second respondent insurance company cannot be exonerated from its liability in paying compensation to the petitioner since the petitioner is a third party and his risk has been covered under Ex.R.2 by collecting additional premium from the insured.

Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.3,55,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. on Rs.3,30,000/-
to the petitioner from the date of the petition till realization.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.

21. Issue No.4 : In view of my findings on the above said issues and for the reasons stated therein , I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER

The claim petition filed by the petitioner is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 and 2, awarding compensation of Rs.3,55,000/- (Rupees three Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
9 lakh fifty five thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., on Rs.3,30,000/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Remaining 50% with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 17th day of January 2024)
(Smt.B.V.RENUKA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bengaluru.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-45-J- 3495 by its rider dashed to the petitioner who was proceeding as pillion rider in the above motorcycle and he sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 09.12.2019?
Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
2 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Merely because there is delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint, the claim of the petitioner cannot be doubted when the complainant has given the plausible explanation for the said delay.
Such being the case, I am of the opinion that merely because there is delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint, the false implication of the insured vehicle cannot be inferred 10.
Hence, even from this document it can be safely held that the petitioner met with an accident and sustained injuries.
It is the duty of the police to visit the hospital to record the statement of the petitioner after receiving the intimation from the hospital authorities, but the police have not done so.
This conduct of the rider of the scooter in question enables the Court to draw an adverse inference against him that as the accident took place due to his negligent act, he has remained silent.
But as discussed above,
the materials placed on record clearly establish that the insured scooter was involved in the accident and the petitioner has sustained injuries on account of accident caused by the rider of the said Honda Activa scooter.
Merely because Ex.P.9(22) is a credit bill and merely because the petitioner has not produced any receipt to show that he has paid the said amount, it cannot be said that the petitioner has not purchased the implants as mentioned in that bill since the medical records discloses that the petitioner has undergone surgery by fixation of Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
5 implants at the fracture site.
As per the admissions of PW2, he has not assessed the whole body disability and functional disability and the petitioner is a Government Doctor and even now the petitioner is working in his hospital.
As per the version of RW1 in the cross-examination,
unnamed person means the person who moves on the two wheeler i.e., either the rider or the pillion rider of the two wheeler.
18. In this case the petitioner met with an accident when he was moving as a pillion rider on Honda Activa Scooter in question due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the said scooter.
Though the policy as per Ex.R.2 is issued as 'Liability only Policy', but the fact that premium has been collected in respect risk of unnamed persons enables the Court to hold that the petitioner who was a pillion rider on the date of accident in the insured scooter comes under unnamed person.
It is pertinent to note that the term 3rd party includes a party other than those who are the parties to the contract of insurance i.e., insurer is one party and the insured is the other party.
Any person other than the two parties comes under the description of 3rd party.
In the present case also, the petitioner is a third party as respondents No.1 and 2 are the parties to the contract of insurance under Ex.R.2.
In view of the version of RW1 that unnamed person means either the rider or the pillion rider of the two wheeler, I am of the opinion that the policy Ex.R.2 covers the risk of the petitioner who was a pillion rider on the insured scooter on the date of accident.
But the situation is not so in the present case, since the second respondent company has collected additional premium towards the risk of unnamed persons.
20. As discussed above, this Court has come to the conclusion that as additional premium has been collected by the second respondent company with respect to an unnamed person under Ex.R.2 , the petitioner who was a pillion rider on the date of accident comes under unnamed person and the risk of the petitioner was covered under the policy Ex.R.2 and as such he is entitled for compensation.
Ex.R.2 was valid as on the date of accident since the accident took place on 09.12.2019.
Merely, on the nomenclature of the policy as 'Liability only Policy', the second respondent insurance company cannot be exonerated from its liability in paying compensation to the petitioner since the petitioner is a third party and his risk has been covered under Ex.R.2 by collecting additional premium from the insured.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.3,55,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. on Rs.3,30,000/-
to the petitioner from the date of the petition till realization.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
21. Issue No.4 : In view of my findings on the above said issues and for the reasons stated therein , I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 and 2, awarding compensation of Rs.3,55,000/- (Rupees three Hoysala H.N vs H.P. Nethra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191832726/
9 lakh fifty five thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., on Rs.3,30,000/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Remaining 50% with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
